transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hello! I'm Dora, and I'm here to help with any questions you may have about your cataract surgery recovery. Have you got any questions about your surgery or recovery so far?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I do have a few questions. Could you tell me when I can start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: According to the information I have, it's recommended to avoid strenuous exercise, including heavy gardening, for a month after surgery. However, you can start with light exercise like brisk walking, gardening, light jogging, and gentle cycling after 1 week. So, it's okay to start with some light gardening after 1 week, but please be careful not to overdo it. Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You should start using preservative-free eye drops for dryness 4 times daily as soon as you get home from the hospital, not eye gel. It's usually recommended to use them 4 times daily to start. If you're running low, you can ask your GP for a refill. Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.intended: Some sensitivity to light is normal after cataract surgery, but if it's severe, especially if your eye is also red and painful, we may need to assess it further. If it's just mild and things seem brighter than usual, wearing sunglasses when you're outside should help. Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you for the information. I don't have any more questions at this time.
